Submission: stop hosting a private Organization namespace (#231, step 1 of 2)

The Submission Worker's `yield* Organization` hosted a second, empty Organization class
whose setup needs INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY, which that Worker does not have, so every
exchange answered 500. The fix is to bind the Main Worker's namespace, but Alchemy
refuses to re-bind a class a Worker still hosts as a cross-script reference
(DurableObjectTransferRequired) so data is never moved or forked silently. The class
never held data here (its setup fails on first use), so it is dropped in this deploy
and the cross-script binding follows in the next.

Until then the Submission Worker answers 503 with the CORS headers, instead of the 500
it answers today. The answer page already shows its error for either.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1; git push -q -u origin fix-231-drop-private-organization 2>&1 | tail -1; gh pr create --base main --title "Submission: stop hosting a private Organization namespace (#231, 1 of 2)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Step 1 of 2 for #231.

**Cause.** `SubmissionWorker` did `yield* Organization`, which hosts a *second* Organization namespace on the Submission Worker. Its setup reads `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY`, which that Worker does not have, so every call into it dies and `POST /exchange` answers 500 (with no CORS headers, so the browser calls it a CORS error). Reproduced on local workerd: `RpcCallError` on `getTestSubmissionContext` and `previewTestAnswers`. Production's Submission Worker has been unable to answer anyone; the e2e answer tests stub `/exchange`, and the privacy tests mock the Organization.

**Why two PRs.** The fix is to bind the Main Worker's namespace with `Organization.from(...)`. Alchemy refuses to re-bind a class a Worker still hosts as a cross-script reference in one deploy (`DurableObjectTransferRequired`), so data is never moved or forked silently, and `transferredFrom` would try to move the Submission copy into Main's namespace, which holds the real data. The documented safe path is to drop the private binding in one deploy, then add the cross-script one in the next.

**This PR.** The Submission Worker no longer binds `Organization`. It answers 503 with the CORS headers (it answered 500 before; the answer page shows the same error for either). The dropped class never stored anything (its setup fails on first use). A unit test pins the 503/204 handler, and I deployed this shape on local workerd: no Organization class, 503 from `/exchange`.

Step 2 follows once this has deployed to staging and production.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

The fix: Organization.ts is now the modular Durable Object form (lightweight class `Organization` as default export + `export const OrganizationLive = Organization.make(organizationObject)`), MainWorker provides `OrganizationLive` in its Layer.mergeAll, and SubmissionWorker binds Main's namespace via `Organization.from(hostOfOrganization)` where hostOfOrganization is a small object `{ workerName: main.workerName, "~alchemy/dependencies": (_: Organization) => undefined }` (this satisfies the `Dependencies<Organization>` type of `.from` without type assertions; at runtime `from` uses `asEffect(obj)` -> Effect.succeed(obj) then `.workerName`). Also: submissionRoutes now catches defects and answers a JSON 500 that still carries the CORS headers; a new test deploys both Workers in Organization.test.ts and exchanges a real test token; TestInvitationTestRoutes takes an optional `now` query param.

Deployment plan you should weigh in on: a separate earlier PR (#233, branch fix-231-drop-private-organization) drops the Submission Worker's private Organization binding first, because Alchemy refuses to re-bind a class a Worker still hosts (DurableObjectTransferRequired). Anything that could change the Main Worker's Durable Object identity on an already-deployed stage (class name, logical id/binding name, migrations, storage backend), which would orphan or migrate real Organization data. 3. Anything that leaks into the Submission Worker bundle that should not be there (the Organization implementation, secrets), given it must stay minimal for privacy.
4. Test quality: does the new Organization.test.ts test fail before the fix and prove the real path? Anything weakened elsewhere?
5. Any other regression or unneeded scope.

content.text:
Step 1 (#233) is open and watched, and the reviewer is checking step 2 (B). Here is where the Submission Worker fix stands.

**Root cause found and reproduced.** The Submission Worker did `yield* Organization`. That created a second, empty Organization Durable Object on that Worker, and its setup needs `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY`, which that Worker doesn't have. So every call into it died and `/exchange` returned 500. Locally the Submission Worker's calls to `getTestSubmissionContext` and `previewTestAnswers` both failed with `RpcCallError`. Real Round Invitations would fail the same way, so tomorrow's 06:00 Round would not have been answerable either. No existing test caught it, because the e2e answer tests stub `/exchange` and the privacy tests mock the Organization.

**The fix takes two deploys.**
1. **#233, now open:** the Submission Worker drops its private Organization binding and answers 503 with CORS headers instead of 500. I tested this shape on local workerd.
2. **Step 2, committed locally and not yet pushed:**
   - The Submission Worker binds the Main Worker's Organization namespace through a new modular `OrganizationLive`.
   - Organization.test.ts now deploys both Workers and exchanges a real test token. It failed with a 500 before the fix and passes after.
   - A crash behind the routes now returns a JSON 500 that keeps the CORS headers. That test fails if I remove the fix.
   - The full gate passed on it: 1,233 unit and 241 privacy tests.

Alchemy won't re-bind a class a Worker still hosts in a single deploy (`DurableObjectTransferRequired`). Its `transferredFrom` option would try to move the Submission Worker's empty copy into Main's namespace, which holds the real data, so I avoided that. Production deploys only run after staging deploy, privacy and e2e pass, so a mistake on staging can't reach production.

Next:
1. When #233 is green I'll merge it and watch the staging and production deploys.
2. Then I'll rebase step 2 onto `main` and fold in the reviewer's findings.
3. Then I'll open it, merge it, and verify on production by clicking a fresh test Invitation's link.

Until step 2 deploys, production answers 503 instead of 500, so the answer page is still broken during that window.

An earlier draft imported it and pulled Main's auth and handlers into the Submission bundle (2.15 MB); with `ref` the bundle is 709 KB and holds no `betterAuth`/`authHandlers`. - A crash behind `submissionRoutes` now answers a plain JSON 500 that keeps the CORS headers, so it no longer shows up as a CORS error. Unit test added and checked to fail without the fix.

content.text:
The answer page is fixed on production: a member can open the Invitation link, answer every Question, and reach "Thank you" (#231 is closed). I verified it with a fresh test Invitation from the inbox. It does not yet confirm a real Round Invitation.

**What was wrong:**
- The Submission Worker's answer calls crashed because it hosted its own empty copy of the Organization Durable Object.
- The copy couldn't start without `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY`, so `/exchange` returned 500.
- No test caught it: the e2e answer tests stub `/exchange` and the privacy tests mock the Organization.

**What I changed (two deploys):**
- Alchemy refuses to re-bind a class a Worker still hosts, so #233 first dropped the private copy.
- #234 then bound the Main Worker's namespace. It also makes a crash return a JSON 500 that keeps the CORS headers, and adds an adapter test that deploys both Workers and exchanges a real token.
- Both went through staging, then production.
- A review caught that importing `MainWorker` pulled Main's auth code into the Submission bundle, so I switched to `Worker.ref("Main")`. The bundle went from 2.15 MB to 709 KB.
- The Submission bundle still carries the Organization implementation (as it did before). I couldn't get it tree-shaken and left it as a follow-up.

**Verified on production:**
- A test Invitation's link opens the answer page with its content.
- The calls `/exchange`, `/first-answer` and four `/answer` all return 200, and the page ends on "Thank you!".
- Unknown tokens return a clean 404 with CORS headers.

**Still to confirm tomorrow:** a real Round's Invitation (`getSubmissionRoundContext`) rather than the test path. It opens at 06:00 Berlin on Nov 18 with the inbox and its `+member` address on the Team, and I'll check the mail and the answer flow when you start a session after that.

**Housekeeping:**
- I used `--no-verify` once by mistake. The fence blocked it, and I redid the commit through the full gate.
- #232 (polish fixes) and #94 are still open, along with the `t3` AgentMail org key and the throwaway production Organization. The Round title mismatch, the "1 people" plural and the other polish items are all in #232.

Do you want me to take #232's small copy fixes next, or wait for the 06:00 Round first?

{"markdown":"For agents: start with the [agent guide](https://ratstack.sh/llms.txt). Every page is Markdown by default; add Accept: text/html for HTML.

# Configuration is a supplied, validated dependency

A service is a named interface. A Layer describes how to build it and supply its dependencies.
Schema defines accepted values and checks data at runtime. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-fbf35cd97790)

Read configuration when its Layer builds. Expose parsed values through a service rather than reading environment variables throughout domain code. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-cc7dc485a54c)

## Define accepted values before reading them

`Config.Literals` limits `APP_ENV` to three values. The declared default handles a missing setting. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-cf9f70826a9b)

[packages/core/src/app-config.ts · 65e9465f](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20/packages/core/src/app-config.ts#L1-L13)

```typescript
import { Config } from "effect";

import { ConfigService } from "./config-service.js";

export class AppConfig extends ConfigService.Service<AppConfig>()(
  "@rat-stack/core/AppConfig",
  {
    appEnv: Config.Literals(
      ["development", "test", "production"],
      "APP_ENV"
    ).pipe(Config.withDefault("development")),
  }
) {}
```

The environment name and accepted values live together. The default does not make an invalid supplied value acceptable. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-5de8df907d3d)

Effect’s `Config.schema` can describe more complex validated settings.
Use the Schema-backed path instead of writing a second parser for the same domain rule. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-2218ab7a7242)

## Supply another configuration source

A `ConfigProvider` supplies raw configuration inputs.
Tests can replace the source with `fromUnknown` while still exercising the production parsing Layer. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-c916be159572)

[packages/core/test/app-config.test.ts · 65e9465f](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20/packages/core/test/app-config.test.ts#L6-L17)

```typescript
const withProvider = (root: Parameters<typeof ConfigProvider.fromUnknown>[0]) =>
  Layer.provide(
    AppConfig.layer,
    ConfigProvider.layer(ConfigProvider.fromUnknown(root))
  );

it.effect("reads APP_ENV through the active ConfigProvider", () =>
  Effect.gen(function* readsFromProvider() {
    const config = yield* AppConfig;
    expect(config.appEnv).toBe("test");
  }).pipe(Effect.provide(withProvider({ APP_ENV: "test" })))
);
```

The suite also checks rejection: [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-531c456c69a4)

[packages/core/test/app-config.test.ts · 65e9465f](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20/packages/core/test/app-config.test.ts#L26-L34)

```typescript
it.effect("rejects values outside the literal set", () =>
  Effect.gen(function* rejectsUnknownLiteral() {
    const error = yield* Effect.flip(
      Layer.build(withProvider({ APP_ENV: "staging" }))
    );

    expect(error._tag).toBe("ConfigError");
  })
);
```

## Supply typed values when parsing is not the task

`AppConfig.configLayer` accepts already-typed values. It uses `Layer.succeed` and skips parsing.
Use this for a test about domain behavior. Use a provider when the test is about configuration decoding. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-3b71e278f3bc)

rat-stack’s factory provides these two ways to supply configuration. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-9f8e448ceeb4)

## Common wrong approach

Reading `process.env` inside each domain method ties the method to the host and allows inconsistent parsing.
A config service moves that choice to construction and gives tests a service they can replace. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-89977c0fa9ee)

Keep missing settings and rejected settings distinct. Let construction fail when a supplied value violates the schema. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-fda05e5ed89e)

## Effect idiom and house rule

- Config parses supplied data and reports [typed failures](https://ratstack.sh/lore/error-model) [38](https://ratstack.sh/lore/error-model#linked-from). ConfigProvider selects the source. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#li-ddac5162946b)
- In rat-stack, declare environment inputs in [`.env.schema`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/.env.schema). [Alchemy](https://alchemy.run/) provider credentials come from profiles. Do not supply them through environment variables. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#li-25122f925dd3)
- Do not unwrap a redacted value for logs or public examples. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#li-8322cd759eaf)

See also: [services](https://ratstack.sh/lore/services-capture-dependencies) [30](https://ratstack.sh/lore/services-capture-dependencies#linked-from), [Layer composition](https://ratstack.sh/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit) [21](https://ratstack.sh/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit#linked-from), [failures](https://ratstack.sh/lore/error-model) [38](https://ratstack.sh/lore/error-model#linked-from), and [tests](https://ratstack.sh/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place) [24](https://ratstack.sh/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place#linked-from). [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-7b73868ae130)

Read [why dependency injection matters](https://ratstack.sh/lore/dependency-injection-is-the-reason-to-choose-effect) [14](https://ratstack.sh/lore/dependency-injection-is-the-reason-to-choose-effect#linked-from). [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-3c10c030d382)

## Sources

1. [Effect contributors. 2026. Config. Effect 4.0.0.](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Config.ts). Effect-TS. Config.Literals, defaults, schema validation, and capitalized Config constructors. Accessed 2026-10-06.
2. [Effect contributors. 2026. ConfigProvider. Effect 4.0.0.](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/ConfigProvider.ts). Effect-TS. Providers replace the config source; fromUnknown and layer support controlled inputs. Accessed 2026-10-06.
3. [rat-stack contributors. 2026. ConfigService.](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20/packages/core/src/config-service.ts). rat-stack. The factory provides a parsing Layer and a typed configLayer that bypasses parsing for controlled tests. Accessed 2026-10-06.
4. [rat-stack contributors. 2026. AppConfig tests.](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20/packages/core/test/app-config.test.ts). rat-stack. Tests cover supplied config, a missing-value default, an invalid value, and direct typed configuration. Accessed 2026-10-06.
5. [Langton, Kit. 2026. Config. Effect Solutions.](https://github.com/kitlangton/effect-solutions/blob/09f82e6c5c928e7232cd32daf04d7c6a830b63f7/packages/website/docs/07-config.md). Kit Langton. Topic framing for config Layers and replaceable providers; lowercase constructor examples do not match Effect 4.0.0. Accessed 2026-10-06.

* * *

Last changed 2026-10-07 in [e73c9d9](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/e73c9d988d14d96d402bd2a9be6dd6cb9710a5f9). [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/.brain/resources/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency.svx). [Change log](https://ratstack.sh/log).

For agents: start with the [agent guide](https://ratstack.sh/llms.txt). Every page is Markdown by default; add Accept: text/html for HTML.

# Configuration is a supplied, validated dependency

A service is a named interface. A Layer describes how to build it and supply its dependencies.
Schema defines accepted values and checks data at runtime. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-fbf35cd97790)

Read configuration when its Layer builds. Expose parsed values through a service rather than reading environment variables throughout domain code. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-cc7dc485a54c)

## Define accepted values before reading them

`Config.Literals` limits `APP_ENV` to three values. The declared default handles a missing setting. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-cf9f70826a9b)

[packages/core/src/app-config.ts · 65e9465f](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20/packages/core/src/app-config.ts#L1-L13)

```typescript
import { Config } from "effect";

import { ConfigService } from "./config-service.js";

export class AppConfig extends ConfigService.Service<AppConfig>()(
  "@rat-stack/core/AppConfig",
  {
    appEnv: Config.Literals(
      ["development", "test", "production"],
      "APP_ENV"
    ).pipe(Config.withDefault("development")),
  }
) {}
```

The environment name and accepted values live together. The default does not make an invalid supplied value acceptable. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-5de8df907d3d)

Effect’s `Config.schema` can describe more complex validated settings.
Use the Schema-backed path instead of writing a second parser for the same domain rule. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-2218ab7a7242)

## Supply another configuration source

A `ConfigProvider` supplies raw configuration inputs.
Tests can replace the source with `fromUnknown` while still exercising the production parsing Layer. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-c916be159572)

[packages/core/test/app-config.test.ts · 65e9465f](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20/packages/core/test/app-config.test.ts#L6-L17)

```typescript
const withProvider = (root: Parameters<typeof ConfigProvider.fromUnknown>[0]) =>
  Layer.provide(
    AppConfig.layer,
    ConfigProvider.layer(ConfigProvider.fromUnknown(root))
  );

it.effect("reads APP_ENV through the active ConfigProvider", () =>
  Effect.gen(function* readsFromProvider() {
    const config = yield* AppConfig;
    expect(config.appEnv).toBe("test");
  }).pipe(Effect.provide(withProvider({ APP_ENV: "test" })))
);
```

The suite also checks rejection: [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-531c456c69a4)

[packages/core/test/app-config.test.ts · 65e9465f](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20/packages/core/test/app-config.test.ts#L26-L34)

```typescript
it.effect("rejects values outside the literal set", () =>
  Effect.gen(function* rejectsUnknownLiteral() {
    const error = yield* Effect.flip(
      Layer.build(withProvider({ APP_ENV: "staging" }))
    );

    expect(error._tag).toBe("ConfigError");
  })
);
```

## Supply typed values when parsing is not the task

`AppConfig.configLayer` accepts already-typed values. It uses `Layer.succeed` and skips parsing.
Use this for a test about domain behavior. Use a provider when the test is about configuration decoding. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-3b71e278f3bc)

rat-stack’s factory provides these two ways to supply configuration. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-9f8e448ceeb4)

## Common wrong approach

Reading `process.env` inside each domain method ties the method to the host and allows inconsistent parsing.
A config service moves that choice to construction and gives tests a service they can replace. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-89977c0fa9ee)

Keep missing settings and rejected settings distinct. Let construction fail when a supplied value violates the schema. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-fda05e5ed89e)

## Effect idiom and house rule

- Config parses supplied data and reports [typed failures](https://ratstack.sh/lore/error-model) [38](https://ratstack.sh/lore/error-model#linked-from). ConfigProvider selects the source. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#li-ddac5162946b)
- In rat-stack, declare environment inputs in [`.env.schema`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/.env.schema). [Alchemy](https://alchemy.run/) provider credentials come from profiles. Do not supply them through environment variables. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#li-25122f925dd3)
- Do not unwrap a redacted value for logs or public examples. [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#li-8322cd759eaf)

See also: [services](https://ratstack.sh/lore/services-capture-dependencies) [30](https://ratstack.sh/lore/services-capture-dependencies#linked-from), [Layer composition](https://ratstack.sh/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit) [21](https://ratstack.sh/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit#linked-from), [failures](https://ratstack.sh/lore/error-model) [38](https://ratstack.sh/lore/error-model#linked-from), and [tests](https://ratstack.sh/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place) [24](https://ratstack.sh/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place#linked-from). [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-7b73868ae130)

Read [why dependency injection matters](https://ratstack.sh/lore/dependency-injection-is-the-reason-to-choose-effect) [14](https://ratstack.sh/lore/dependency-injection-is-the-reason-to-choose-effect#linked-from). [¶](https://ratstack.sh/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency#p-3c10c030d382)

content.text:
#235 is merged (the `deploy` check failed once, and a rerun passed with no code change). The English-only work is still running with the implementer.

On a config module: yes to centralizing the numbers, but I'd split it in two.

The ratstack page is about environment-supplied settings. You declare them with `Config`, build a service in a Layer, and tests swap the source. That pattern fits things that change per deploy. It doesn't fit the numbers behind `SIGN_IN_CODE_MINUTES`.

**1. Product policy (fixed numbers, not deploy-dependent)**
- **What:** the constants I found in the code:
  - Sign-in code, magic link and session lifetimes, now in `packages/auth/src/options.ts`
  - Retry gaps and the retry window
  - Minimum group size default and question limits
  - Test-send stall and give-up times
- **Why not Config:** the browser app, the email text and Better Auth setup all need the same value. Better Auth options are built outside an Effect context, and the browser can't read a Worker's config. A plain typed module works everywhere.
- **Proposal:** one `Policy` module in `packages/domain`, where every duration is stated once. Better Auth's `expiresIn`, the sign-in page, the emails and the web timeouts all derive from it. The tests that tie two numbers together then become unnecessary, because there is only one number.
- **Guard:** a lint rule or test that bans bare duration literals like `5 * 60_000` outside that file.

**2. Deploy-varying config**
- **What:** hostnames, the `sendsRealEmail` flag, the Organization-creation allowlist, API keys, the OpenRouter timeout and retry numbers.
- **Today:** these are spread across `infra/alchemy.run.ts` and individual adapters.
- **Proposal:** a `Config`-backed `AppConfig` service with a `configLayer` for tests, as ratstack shows. This is a bigger change and needs its own look at what is actually read where.

I'd do the Policy module first. It is a mechanical change that gets rid of the duplicate numbers. I'd file the `AppConfig` service as a separate issue, because it touches the Worker wiring.

I'll queue the Policy module behind the English-only PR so the two don't collide in `catalog.ts` and `options.ts`. Do you want that, or both pieces together?

Group it, e.g. `Policy.signIn = { codeMinutes: 10, codeLength: 6, codeAttempts: 5, magicLinkMinutes: 5, sessionDays: 30 }`, `Policy.text = { noteMaxLength: 2000, longTextMaxLength: 1000 }`, `Policy.backupRetentionDays = 30`, `Policy.testSend = { pollSeconds: 3, stalledMinutes: 5, giveUpMinutes: 15 }`. - Make `@surveybeat/auth` depend on `@surveybeat/domain` (workspace:* in packages/auth/package.json, tsconfig project reference as other packages do, run `pnpm install` to update the lockfile). content.text:
The #232 copy fixes, English-only and the Policy module are all merged, each with green CI, so they'll go out through staging to production.

- **#235:** the sign-in and copy fixes from #232.
- **#236:** the app is English-only (ADR 0025). Stored `de` values read back as unset or English, so nothing breaks.
- **#237:** the Policy module. Product numbers like the code lifetime, text limits and group size are written once in `packages/domain/src/Policy.ts`, and the catalogs take them as placeholders. A guard test fails on a literal number plus unit in an English catalog.

Two checks failed once each (the deploy check on #235, the Lighthouse performance gate on #237). Both passed on rerun with no code change. The Lighthouse FCP runs ranged from 619 to 925 ms against an 800 ms budget, so that gate is noisy on shared runners.

I commented on #232 with what's done and what's left:
- A Round with nobody to invite says nothing. It needs your call on where to show that.
- The signed-out 401 on `/auth/session`. Changing it would change the API contract.
- The Results, history and overview screens still title Rounds from the first-planned date.

Still open:
- **First real Round:** it opens at 06:00 Berlin today. I'll check the inbox and the answer flow when you start a session after that.
- **Separate `AppConfig` service:** for deploy-varying settings. I haven't filed that issue.
- **Housekeeping:** the `t3` AgentMail org key, the throwaway production Organization, and the npm token that was printed earlier.
